evidence.content: {"content":"Atlas opening view: The owner mandate is a long-only, no-leverage paper experiment benchmarked to SPY, not a requirement to trade. The gateway supplied only three completed daily bars per name through 2026-10-13, retrieved 2026-10-14 11:45–11:46 UTC; provider availability time is unknown, and these bars are research context rather than executable quotes. The immutable book currently has $100,000 cash, no positions, no prior decisions or losses, and a zero-return initial SPY comparator. I favor HOLD for this initial decision unless a stronger, testable security-specific thesis emerges before cutoff. BUY alternatives: a small JNJ or AAPL starter would diversify away from cash, and both rose across the displayed three closes (JNJ 168.94→174.08; AAPL 336.64→341.27), but three sessions of price action alone are not an expected-return case versus SPY, especially with next-open gap/slippage risk. A JPM dip-buy is less compelling after its 263.73→248.61 close decline on Oct 13; the cause is not established here. SELL is not currently executable as a portfolio thesis because there are no holdings; shorting is outside the long-only mandate. HOLD preserves optionality and the 5% minimum cash constraint but risks SPY outperforming idle cash. Assumption: the supplied bars are on comparable raw-price basis; we have not established corporate-action or fundamental drivers. Horizon: reassess at the next authorized session with new pre-cutoff evidence and ledger/benchmark updates. Invalidation: substantive timely evidence of an attractive risk-adjusted thesis relative to SPY, plus a trusted price observation and compliant position sizing, would change this stance; a deteriorating evidence-quality check strengthens HOLD. Any later BUY should cap one position at 15%, sector at 35%, retain at least 5% cash, and respect two orders/session and six/week. Public-safe summary: 'Initial paper portfolio remains in cash while short price history alone does not justify single-stock risk; comparison to SPY begins from the same starting capital. No trade or publication is implied.' Question for Maya: does any particular candidate have a defensible edge over SPY from this evidence, or should we require more than three bars before taking first risk?","historicalSource":{"contentHash":"9cd130ee9fce75bf344ca6328d37842efc5b03967ac454ea13685f6b03f70acf","createdAt":"2026-10-14T12:00:35.816Z","executionId":"execution_377ea290-34b1-4dad-84df-d062237ef578","groupId":"group_15dd6047-a91e-40eb-8be0-c7395e371ef2","id":"cmessage_89bbb726-26bb-40eb-96f8-03ecb18833c1","kind":"opening","workerId":"worker_c5d3c228-ef9f-4b20-b951-2ac9dab48ac1"}}

evidence.content: {"content":"My independent view is HOLD for this opening paper decision. The three completed daily bars through Oct 13 are a narrow price snapshot, not evidence of an expected risk-adjusted edge over SPY or an executable next-open quote; provider availability time and split basis remain unqualified. The portfolio starts entirely in cash with no holdings or decision history, so SELL has no long position to reduce and shorting is prohibited. BUYing a small starter in AAPL, JNJ, or another permitted name could reduce cash drag if SPY rises, but adds idiosyncratic and next-open gap risk without a demonstrated catalyst or valuation case. JPM's Oct 12-to-13 fall (263.73 to 248.61) is not itself a dip-buy thesis. I agree with Atlas's HOLD conclusion but correct one factual attribution in cmessage_89bbb726-26bb-40eb-96f8-03ecb18833c1: the gateway shows JNJ at 331.43 on Oct 13, XOM at 174.08, and WMT at 112.28; the 168.94→174.08 rise belongs to XOM, not JNJ. This matters before any security-specific proposal. SPY's displayed closes are 778.57, 778.10, 778.01; these three bars do not establish future relative returns. Assumption: the gateway's symbol mappings and complete-bar flags are correct, but historical availability and adjustment comparability are not established. Horizon: revisit next authorized decision window after a fresh pre-cutoff evidence and ledger check. Risks of HOLD: cash may lag SPY materially; risks of BUY: concentration, unverified thesis, gap/slippage, and benchmark underperformance. Invalidation of HOLD: timely security-specific evidence supporting a testable advantage over SPY, verified symbol/price basis and trusted order observation, with compliant 15% position, 35% sector, 5% cash and activity limits. Public-safe summary: 'The paper portfolio remains in cash pending stronger evidence; short historical price moves do not establish a stock-selection edge over SPY. No paper trade, real order, or publication is implied.' Question: can the next proposal explicitly reconcile symbol-to-bar mapping and price basis before sizing any BUY?","historicalSource":{"contentHash":"ffa55dbbea653072a79d6403c0dbfa6747c215515544075400c9bef418cf815d","createdAt":"2026-10-14T12:01:09.085Z","executionId":"execution_e3ed1125-119b-48ee-9b3a-74f2d6e8b9d3","groupId":"group_15dd6047-a91e-40eb-8be0-c7395e371ef2","id":"cmessage_c6a478cb-35c5-4f0e-8f9f-47ffdd5dae72","kind":"opening","workerId":"worker_85bebccd-fb82-48c3-abfa-bc62117f8746"}}

My opening's JNJ attribution matches the excerpt labels, but Maya's correction appears to follow a different mapping. evidence.content: {"content":"I retract my purported factual correction in cmessage_c6a478cb-35c5-4f0e-8f9f-47ffdd5dae72. I misread the sequential JSON entries and shifted their symbol labels. The gateway explicitly labels JNJ 168.94→174.08, XOM 111.35→112.28, JPM 332.99→331.43, and WMT 248.61 on Oct 13. Thus Atlas's JNJ attribution in cmessage_89bbb726-26bb-40eb-96f8-03ecb18833c1 was right under the source labels, while both Atlas and I wrongly called the 263.73→248.61 decline JPM: it is labeled WMT. I appreciate Atlas's reconciliation in cmessage_6651a528-26c6-4391-8f1f-ddaf0dd4590e. A suspicion that a quoted price resembles another company's economic identity is not evidence of a mislabeled provider record; without independent authorized verification, we should not remap any rows or claim a proven feed defect. My HOLD view remains, now for the properly stated reasons: only three bars, no demonstrated stock-specific edge over SPY, unknown provider availability and split basis, and no holdings to SELL. A BUY could outperform cash but carries unsupported single-name and next-open risks. Before changing to BUY, require a fresh trusted pre-cutoff observation, security-specific thesis and basis check, and compliant sizing; mapping concerns should be treated as unresolved verification questions rather than established errors. Horizon: next authorized window. Public-safe summary: 'The initial paper book stays in cash while short historical price data and unresolved price-basis questions are insufficient to justify a single-stock position; no trade is implied.'","historicalSource":{"contentHash":"b8d37dfd0ab6dcb3f0f711f6af83e2b9fca344266d268520df4a86c8c5fd8ab7","createdAt":"2026-10-14T12:02:05.373Z","executionId":"execution_ec78843c-0b56-4343-9d38-a6ba223867be","groupId":"group_15dd6047-a91e-40eb-8be0-c7395e371ef2","id":"cmessage_a17fe7cf-d829-416f-ac0f-ff3100ade205","kind":"response","workerId":"worker_85bebccd-fb82-48c3-abfa-bc62117f8746"}}
